transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-15 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Kim (Redwood CSM), Diego Mendez (Redwood SE), Rohit Sen (Redwood Platform), Lena Ortiz (Tamarisk), Samir Patel (Tamarisk), Priya Rao (Tamarisk Security), Evan Chu (Tamarisk SRE)

Auto-generated summary: Kickoff run through, pilot scope agreed, security docs requested.

[00:00] Ava: hi everyone, thanks for joining, um this is the kickoff for the Tamarisk implementation, I'll run through agenda real quick, then pass to Diego for tech overview, and Rohit will cover networking and staging.
[00:20] Lena: thanks Ava, really excited, we want to get a two week pilot running asap to validate latency and cost tradeoffs for our inference workloads.
[00:33] Diego: cool, quick intro on our side - Diego, solutions eng; we've done a bunch of pilots similar to this. For Tamarisk specifically we looked at your perf doc, um curious about batch sizes and typical prompt lengths.
[00:48] Samir: our median user prompt is about 120 tokens, but we have long tails up to 2K tokens for certain workflows. Latency target is sub-300ms for median, cost target is... well, we'd like cost to be competitive with our current provider.
[01:10] Priya: security is my focus - we need to ensure data encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, and audit logs. Also SSO (SAML) for our users.
[01:32] Rohit: noted, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, and we can run Redwood Private in a VPC or on-prem if needed. There was a note about data residency - can you clarify, Lena?
[01:45] Lena: primary data in us-east, but we're evaluating eu-west for GDPR-sensitive subsets. So we need to see region options and controls.
[02:05] Diego: for the pilot we'll suggest using a hosted staging environment with VPC peering so you can test network egress and latency. If you need air-gapped, we can discuss Private on prem later.
[02:25] Evan: on the SRE side we want network diagrams and firewall ports up front, also sample traffic patterns.
[02:40] Diego: yeah we'll share a peering checklist. For perf: do you have a sample dataset and traffic pattern we can run?
[02:52] Samir: yes, we'll share a 10k request sample and a smaller subset for latency.
[03:05] Ava: goals for this call - confirm pilot scope, agree owners, and next steps. Items to confirm: success criteria (latency/cost), security sign-off path, timeline.
[03:22] Priya: security sign-off will require our InfoSec and legal reviews; SOC2 plus network isolation is a must.
[03:34] Rohit: understood. Quick question on keys - do you prefer customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed during the pilot?
[03:45] Priya: prefer customer-managed, but we can allow Redwood-managed in staging for speed, as long as we have plan to rotate to our KMS before prod.
[03:58] Diego: that's common. We'll do staging with Redwood-managed keys unless you insist otherwise. We'll document rotation steps.
[04:10] Lena: timeline - we want pilot to kick off next Monday if possible. Is that realistic?
[04:18] Ava: timeline looks tight but doable if we get artifacts (sample dataset, network contacts, security questionnaire) by Friday.
[04:32] Samir: action from our side - Samir will send sample payloads; Priya will share the security checklist.
[04:45] Evan: also want routing and egress cost visibility, like per-token cost breakdown in the console.
[04:55] Diego: console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model. We'll set up a demo for that in the deep-dive.
[05:08] Lena: one concern is fallback behavior if capacity is constrained - can Redwood route to cheaper variants automatically?
[05:18] Rohit: yes, we have smart routing and fallback policies; you can set policies by latency or cost. We'll show examples.
[05:30] Samir: about observability - logs, traces, and prompt-level tracing - is that available?
[05:38] Diego: yes, per-route dashboards, traces, error analysis; note that prompt-level data retention is configurable for privacy.
[05:50] Priya: we need audit logs retained for 2 years per finance/regulatory. Is that supported?
[05:58] Rohit: we can set retention windows and export to your S3, plus provide audit logs for export.
[06:12] Ava: ok let's walk the pilot scope - objectives, success criteria, and 2-week plan.
[06:20] Ava: Objective 1: validate latency target of sub-300ms median for baseline workload. Objective 2: quantify cost per 1k tokens and compare. Success criteria: median latency < 300ms 95% of the time; cost within 20% of current provider.
[06:47] Samir: that sounds reasonable. We'll provide the benchmark dataset and expected SLA.
[06:58] Diego: technical notes - model selection: we'll suggest an optimized open model and a quantized variant for cost testing; A/B testing against your current supplier is doable.
[07:15] Lena: are there restrictions on prompt pre-processing or de-dup caches? We do prefix caching in our stack.
[07:24] Diego: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching and continuous batching; we can tune cache TTLs and batch windows. Some of the kernel selection heuristics are automatic but we can expose parameters.
[07:40] Priya: legal will want a data processing addendum for the pilot.
[07:46] Ava: we'll loop legal in, and I'll share the DPA template.
[07:54] Evan: network - latency concern between our eu-west users and us-east region; can we test eu-west?
[08:03] Rohit: yes, we support regions; for pilot we can spin up instances in eu-west, but cost and provisioning time needs to be discussed.
[08:18] Samir: what about dedicated capacity vs hosted? For predictable throughput, Dedicated is better but more costly.
[08:28] Diego: correct - Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; Hosted is faster to start. For the pilot we recommend hosted with reserved burst capacity if you need consistent latencies.
[08:44] Lena: ok default to hosted for pilot, but we want recommendations on when to move to Dedicated.
[08:53] Diego: we'll provide quant recommendations tied to workload; Optimize toolkit will suggest quantization and batching settings.
[09:05] Priya: encryption - can we get HSM-backed KMS?
[09:11] Rohit: supported in Private deployments; for hosted we can integrate your cloud KMS via customer-managed keys. HSM requires additional setup.
[09:22] Samir: compliance question - do you have SOC2 Type II report?
[09:27] Ava: yes, we'll share the SOC2 pack; it's in the security folder and we'll include it in the security pack.
[09:40] Lena: great. Any blockers we foresee?
[09:45] Priya: none immediate, just legal review timeline could push to next week.
[09:51] Ava: ok moving on - onboarding steps: staging access, API keys, SSO, role creation.
[10:00] Diego: we'll provision a staging org, with role-based access - you can map SAML groups to roles.
[10:12] Evan: provisioning times?
[10:15] Rohit: staging org can be up within 24-48 hours once we have contacts and the account owner.
[10:24] Samir: about cost reporting - we'd like token-level granularity and per-route annotations for our billing.
[10:34] Diego: console supports per-route cost. We can add tags so you can map to internal billing.
[10:44] Lena: next is runbook - what does rollback look like during pilot?
[10:49] Diego: rollback is basically route traffic back to your existing provider or to a fallback model; we can automate canaries and automatic fallback for errors or latency breaches.
[11:03] Priya: we will need a stop-gap SLA in the pilot for availability if we do critical traffic.
[11:10] Ava: we can include a pilot-level availability target but full SLA is part of Dedicated contracts.
[11:20] Evan: curious about token accounting - how do we measure subtle differences in tokenization?
[11:26] Diego: we'll run the same tokenizer pipeline; differences are small but we'll flag any parity issues.
[11:34] Samir: any red flags about integrating with our infra?
[11:37] Rohit: visible ones are network, KMS, and SSO - all standard. We'll send templates.
[11:46] Lena: ok let's capture clear owners and due dates.
[11:50] Ava: (recap) Owners: Diego - perf bench; Rohit - network diagram; Ava - security pack and runbook; Samir/Priya - provide datasets and security answers.
[12:05] Priya: legal will need two business days to review the DPA once sent.
[12:10] Ava: action items noted. Any final questions?
[12:18] Lena: none from me. Thank you.
[12:22] Samir: thanks team.
[12:25] Diego: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and share docs.

Meeting end. Recap:
- Pilot: 2-week, hosted staging with VPC peering, aim to start next Monday if artifacts delivered by Friday.
- Security pack and SOC2 to be shared by Redwood (Ava) by 2025-03-17.
- Perf benchmark to run by Diego with dataset from Samir - due 2025-03-22.
- Network/VPC diagram and peering checklist from Rohit - due 2025-03-19.
- Next meeting: 60-min technical deep-dive (SRE + SE) to be scheduled in next 3 business days.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription missed some technical acronyms and sometimes split speaker labels; please refer to meeting notes for precise config snippets.
